The driver chose a different frame interval.

The result of a write: what was asked, what the device actually holds, and why they
differ if they do (design D3/E4).

Every layer above preserves both fields. A layer that collapses them to one value is
dropping the fact the whole doctrine exists to keep (rubric A10).

Which backend a camera came from.

Closed on purpose: each composition root holds one exhaustive `match` over this

Something else, described. Free-text is deliberate: the alternative is a closed

CameraDetail.description: What `info` answers: one camera and the formats its capture node offers.

Formats, with sizes and the intervals available at each size nested under them

CameraFingerprint.description:
Best-effort identity across replug and reboot.

Serial numbers are in here but not trusted: the Chicony reports `"0001"` and the
OBSBOT reports none at all [PF:8]. Matching is conservative — a mismatch on
`calibrate apply` is a refusal naming the differing fields, not a warning.

CameraId.description:
The name RPC calls and CLI arguments use: `cam:<card-slug>[-<n>]`.

Reproducible across runs while the attached topology is unchanged, and stable for one
engine's lifetime even across replug. Never persisted as identity — that is
[`CameraFingerprint`]'s job.

CameraInfo.description: A camera: a group of nodes, an identity, and the driver's own description of itself.

backend.description:
Which backend produced this. Recorded so `--json` output is self-describing and
a fake-backend run can never be mistaken for a hardware one.

fingerprint.description: The identity that survives a replug.

nodes.description: Every node in the group, capture and metadata alike.

hints.description: Anything worth saying about what is *not* in the list.

ControlDesc.description: Everything the device says about one control.

current.description:
The current value **as read, unvalidated** — outside the range is a fact about
the device, not an error to correct [PF:4]. `None` when it was not read (a
write-only control, or an enumeration that did not fetch values).

default.description: The declared default — which may sit outside `range` [PF:5].

dims.description: Array dimensions, when the control is one.

elems.description: Element count for arrays and compound controls (1 for scalars).

menu.description: Menu items by index. Sparse [PF:2]; empty for non-menu controls.

slug.description: The name through the D2 transform.

ControlFlags.description: A control's flags: the raw word and the decoded subset, both preserved.

known.description: The bits this version can name, in declaration order.

unknown_bits.description: The bits it cannot. Not an error, not dropped — next year's flag is data.

ControlId.description: A V4L2 control id (`V4L2_CID_*`), as the kernel numbers it.

ControlRange.description:
A control's declared range. Declared: the current value and the default are both
free to sit outside it, and on real hardware they do [PF:4, PF:5].

step.description:
Declared step. Zero and negative steps occur; treat them as 1 when planning
(see [`ControlRange::effective_step`]) rather than dividing by them.

camera.description: Which camera these came from — so a saved `--json` document is self-describing.

controls.description:
Every control the device enumerated, including the ones this build cannot
interpret [PF:1].

pairs.description:
The auto/manual pairs in effect for this camera (design D3): the declared table
filtered to controls this device has, merged with anything a probe measured on it.

Each pair carries its own [`crate::pairing::Provenance`], because "the UVC spec
says so" and "this camera did it while we watched" are different claims and E1
makes the second one win.

ControlRole.description: What part a control plays in restore ordering.

oneOf.description:
An automation control — restored first, so it is in place before the manual
values it governs.
Everything else.

ControlSession.description: One control's whole story within a session.

ControlSlug.description:
A control's slug: its kernel name through the D2 transform, the spelling agents and
`v4l2-ctl` users already know.

ControlStatus.description: Where one control stands in a session (design D8's closed vocabulary).

oneOf.description: Nothing has happened to it yet.
Its automation partner has been disabled and its value parked.

automation.description: The automation controls that were switched off.

parked_value.description: The value the control holds while parked.

oneOf.description: A sweep is in progress.
A value has been chosen.

precision.description:
The final sampling step — the skill's "calibration precision". Multi-pass
refinement (coarse then fine) is representable because this is recorded.

score.description: The score that value earned, when a metric produced one.

oneOf.description: Deliberately set aside.
Cannot be calibrated on this device.

ControlType.description:
A control's type.

Closed for the types we can interpret, open-ended for the rest: `Unknown` carries the
raw discriminant so a control we cannot read still enumerates, displays, round-trips,
and is reported by name. The Chicony's `Region of Interest Rectangle` (type `0x0107`)
is the seed case — the crate that panicked on it is why we own this layer [PF:1].

oneOf.description: `V4L2_CTRL_TYPE_INTEGER`
`V4L2_CTRL_TYPE_BOOLEAN`
`V4L2_CTRL_TYPE_MENU` — items are named strings, sparsely indexed [PF:2].
`V4L2_CTRL_TYPE_BUTTON` — write-only trigger, no value.
`V4L2_CTRL_TYPE_INTEGER64`
`V4L2_CTRL_TYPE_CTRL_CLASS` — a class header, not a real control.
`V4L2_CTRL_TYPE_STRING`
`V4L2_CTRL_TYPE_BITMASK`
`V4L2_CTRL_TYPE_INTEGER_MENU` — items are integers, sparsely indexed.
`V4L2_CTRL_TYPE_U8` — compound array of bytes.
`V4L2_CTRL_TYPE_U16` — compound array.
`V4L2_CTRL_TYPE_U32` — compound array.
`V4L2_CTRL_TYPE_AREA` — `{width, height}`.
`V4L2_CTRL_TYPE_RECT` — `{left, top, width, height}`; the PF:1 control.

Anything else the kernel emits: carried as an opaque payload.

The payload's size is on the descriptor (`elem_size` × `elems`), not here — one
home per fact.

ControlValue.description:
A control value, as read or as written.

Three shapes, not fifteen: scalars are integers whatever their declared type, and
interpretation is the descriptor's job. Payload types are opaque bytes, which is
exactly enough to round-trip a control we cannot read.

oneOf.description: Integer, boolean, menu index, bitmask — anything scalar.
`V4L2_CTRL_TYPE_STRING`.
A compound or unrecognized payload, byte-exact.

DeviceNode.description: One `/dev/videoN` node belonging to a camera.

capabilities.description:
The whole-device `capabilities` word, kept because it differs from `device_caps`
on multi-node devices and the difference is the point.

Error.description: Everything that can go wrong, as a value the caller can branch on.

oneOf.description: The device disappeared — unplugged, or the driver unbound.
Another process holds the device. Distinct from "the camera cannot do this" (E3).

holders.description: Who has it, when `/proc` was readable.

oneOf.description: The device node exists but we may not open it. The hint lives here, once.
No camera matched the id or prefix.
Several cameras matched the prefix.
No control by that slug or id.

did_you_mean.description: The closest slugs this camera does have.

oneOf.description: The control exists and cannot be written [PF:12].

An automation partner currently owns the control [PF:3]. Actionable: the
variant names the control to disable.

automation.description: The automation control to disable first, when one was discovered.

oneOf.description: The requested pixel format is not one this camera offers.

requested.description: What was asked for, when the caller named something.

oneOf.description: Frames kept arriving but the settle policy never converged [PF:11].

frames_seen.description: How many frames arrived in that time — zero means a different problem.

oneOf.description: The camera is not the one this session was recorded against.
Another session already owns this (camera, task) pair.
The calibration state machine refused a transition (design D8).
A persisted document was written by a version we do not understand (D9).
The state directory's advisory lock is held elsewhere (D9).

holder.description: Who holds it, when we could tell.

oneOf.description: `terminate_holder` was asked to kill a pid that no longer holds the device.

pid.description: The pid named in the request.

oneOf.description:
The kernel refused an operation for a reason with no more specific home.

Deliberately typed rather than stringly: `operation` and `errno` are what a
caller (or a bug report) actually needs. See note N4.
A filesystem operation on the state directory failed (disk full, and friends).

The operation exists in the contract and this build does not perform it yet.

Emphatically **not** a capability answer (E3): the device was never asked. A
half-built backend has to say something when a trait method it has not reached
is called, and every other choice is worse — a panic breaks the "plugging in a
webcam cannot panic the library" rule, and reusing [`Error::DeviceIo`] would
blame the kernel for our own schedule. See note N6.

arrives_in.description: The phase that lands it, in docs/2's spelling (`P2`).

operation.description: The trait method or verb that was called.

FormatInfo.description:
One pixel format and everything available in it.

Nesting is load-bearing: the OBSBOT offers MJPG up to 3840×2160 while YUYV stops at
640×480 on the same cable, so a flat size list would be a lie [PF:9].

sizes.description: Sizes, each with its own intervals.

FrameInterval.description: A frame interval (the reciprocal of a frame rate — the kernel's own convention).

oneOf.description: One exact interval, as a fraction of a second.
A range with a step.

An interval described with a `v4l2_frmivaltypes` value this build cannot interpret.
Carried for [`FrameSize::Unknown`]'s reason.

FrameSize.description: A frame size the device offers.

oneOf.description: One exact size.
A range with a step.

A size described with a `v4l2_frmsizetypes` value this build cannot interpret.

D2's rule, applied to sizes: the entry exists, so it is carried. Dropping it would
make a *short* size list look like a complete one, and "this camera does not offer
4K" is exactly the capability claim we would be inventing.

FrameSizeInfo.description: A frame size together with the intervals available *at that size*.

HintKind.description:
Why a listing might not say what the user expected.

D1: "an empty enumeration is diagnosed, not shrugged at". Hints are *data*, not
prose the CLI prints and the daemon forgets — an agent reading `--json` gets the
same diagnosis a human reading the table does.

oneOf.description:
A USB device presents a video-class interface and no driver has bound a V4L2
node to it — the skill's `lsusb` triage, built in [PF:14].

A device node exists and could not be interrogated, so the camera it belongs
to is not in the listing.

The alternative — listing the camera with only the nodes that answered —
would let a busy capture node read as "this camera cannot capture", which is
the availability-as-capability conversion E3 exists to prevent.

Holder.description:
A process holding a device open, as diagnosed from `/proc/*/fd` — the `fuser`
replacement. Killing one is a separate explicit command, never a side effect
(design §5, D10).

comm.description: Its `comm`, when `/proc` let us read it.

KnownFlag.description:
The control flag bits this version names.

Flags are carried as raw bits *plus* this decoded set, because the set grows:
`HasWhichMinMax` (0x1000) arrived with the same kernel work as the RECT support
behind PF:1 and older references do not list it [PF:12]. Bits outside this
vocabulary survive in [`ControlFlags::unknown_bits`].

oneOf.description: `V4L2_CTRL_FLAG_DISABLED` — permanently unsupported on this device.
`V4L2_CTRL_FLAG_GRABBED` — busy because streaming is in progress.
`V4L2_CTRL_FLAG_READ_ONLY` — the Chicony's `Privacy` control [PF:12].
`V4L2_CTRL_FLAG_UPDATE` — writing it changes other controls' properties.
`V4L2_CTRL_FLAG_INACTIVE` — an automation partner owns it right now [PF:3].
`V4L2_CTRL_FLAG_SLIDER` — a UI hint.
`V4L2_CTRL_FLAG_WRITE_ONLY` — reading it is meaningless.
`V4L2_CTRL_FLAG_VOLATILE` — the value changes without us writing it.
`V4L2_CTRL_FLAG_HAS_PAYLOAD` — the value is a compound payload.
`V4L2_CTRL_FLAG_EXECUTE_ON_WRITE` — writing has an effect beyond the value.
`V4L2_CTRL_FLAG_MODIFY_LAYOUT` — writing it reshapes the format.
`V4L2_CTRL_FLAG_DYNAMIC_ARRAY` — element count varies at runtime.
`V4L2_CTRL_FLAG_HAS_WHICH_MIN_MAX` — widely set on recent kernels [PF:12].

ListHint.description: One diagnosis attached to a listing.

kind.description: What kind of problem this is.

subject.description: What it is about — a USB device path such as `1-2`.

oneOf.description: The session was created.
The pre-sweep snapshot was persisted.
An automation control was switched off.

manual.description: The manual control this was for.

oneOf.description: A sweep began.
A sample was recorded.
A sweep finished.

samples.description: How many samples were actually taken.

oneOf.description: A value was chosen.
The session's values were applied to a camera.
The camera was put back as found.

restored.description: How many controls came back exactly.

MenuItem.description:
One menu item. Menus are sparse: `VIDIOC_QUERYMENU` returns `EINVAL` on the holes,
and the holes are real [PF:2].

oneOf.description: A named item (`V4L2_CTRL_TYPE_MENU`), e.g. `"Manual Mode"`.

name.description: The kernel's name for this index.

oneOf.description: An integer item (`V4L2_CTRL_TYPE_INTEGER_MENU`).

value.description: The kernel's value for this index.

oneOf.description: Variance of the Laplacian: higher is sharper.
Fraction of pixels at or near full white. Higher means more blown highlights.
Fraction of pixels at or near full black.
Mean luma, 0.0–1.0. Neither high nor low is "better" — it is context.
Root-mean-square contrast.

NegotiatedStream.description: What the device actually agreed to.

adjustments.description:
Every way this differs from what was asked. Empty means the request was honored
exactly — and an empty list is a claim, so it is reported rather than assumed.

bytes_per_line.description: Bytes per row, as the driver reports it (0 for compressed formats).

pixel_format.description: The format frames will arrive in.

size_image.description: The driver's maximum frame size in bytes.

NodeKind.description: What a device node is for, decided by `device_caps` [PF:7].

oneOf.description: `V4L2_CAP_VIDEO_CAPTURE` — frames come from here.
`V4L2_CAP_META_CAPTURE` — recorded, never streamed.
`V4L2_CAP_VIDEO_OUTPUT` — an output node on the same interface.
Something else. Represented, not discarded.

device_caps.description: The `device_caps` word that produced this classification.

PhotoDelivery.description:
Where a photo's bytes ended up — [`Sink`], answered.

The two variants pair with the two sinks, and each says the thing its caller cannot
otherwise learn: a path answer reports how much was written, and a bytes answer reports
how much is on its way. **The bytes themselves are not in this document**: `wch` streams
them to standard output, and D10's base64-in-JSON encoding lands at P4 with the wire
surface that needs it (docs/2 puts the sink DTO in `webcam-handler-api`). Carrying an
unused encoding here would be a dependency nobody reads.

oneOf.description: The bytes were handed back to the caller.
The bytes were written to a file.

PhotoFormat.description: The encoding a photo lands in.

oneOf.description: JPEG. Verbatim camera bytes when the stream is already MJPG (E6), else encoded.
PNG. Always encoded, always lossless.
Binary PPM/PGM — the "give me pixels" escape hatch for tooling.

PhotoRendering.description:
What the photo pipeline did to produce a photo's bytes (design D6/E6).

Reported alongside every photo because "the camera's own bitstream" and "a faithful
re-encode" are different products, and a calibration sample that was re-encoded is
partly ranking our codec rather than the lens.

oneOf.description: The camera's own bitstream, byte for byte (E6).

source.description: The format the camera delivered, which is the format on disk.

oneOf.description: A compressed frame was decoded and encoded again.
A raw frame was converted to pixels and encoded.

PhotoReport.description:
What `photo` answers (design D6).

Self-describing on purpose: a saved `--json` document says which camera, when, what the
device actually agreed to stream, and whether the bytes are the camera's own — the four
things a calibration sample or a bug report needs and cannot reconstruct later.

frames_settled.description: How many frames were discarded before this one [PF:11].

negotiated.description: What the device agreed to, including every way that differs from the request (D5).

rendering.description: Which of D6's three paths produced the bytes.

width.description: The width of the image the bytes encode, after any pixel-domain transform.

PhotoRequest.description:
Everything one photo needs (design D5, D6, D10).

Assembled by the caller so `wch photo`, the daemon's `photo` method and a calibration
sample all ask for a photo the same way — the sweep at P3 varies the control values
between shots and nothing else.

settle.description: How long to let the sensor settle first [PF:11].

stream.description: What to ask the device's format negotiation for.

transform.description: The orientation, applied to pixels or recorded in EXIF depending on the sink (E6).

PixelFormat.description: A pixel format, as its FourCC.

ProfileInvariant.description: The part of a profile that should not change unless the device or the kernel does.

controls.description:
The full control set, with `current` cleared and the volatile flag bits masked
out — see [`invariant_control`].

formats.description: Formats, with sizes and intervals nested [PF:9].

measured_pairs.description: Automation pairs discovered by probing this device [PF:3].

ProfileProvenance.description:
Where a profile came from. Never compared — a re-capture has a new timestamp by
definition.

backend.description:
Which backend produced it. A profile captured from the fake backend would be
circular corpus, so this field is what makes that visible.

capturer.description: Who or what ran the capture.

tool_version.description: The tool version that captured it.

ProfileState.description: The part that changes with use.

flags.description:
Each control's raw flag word at capture time. The INACTIVE bit here tracks which
automation was on when the profile was taken [PF:3].

values.description:
Each control's value at capture time — including the ones outside their declared
range [PF:4], which is exactly why this is recorded.

Provenance.description: Where a claim about this device came from.

oneOf.description: Transcribed from documentation. Nominated, not legislated.
Observed on this device, by probe. Beats `Declared` on conflict (E1).

Written, with the usual `{requested, applied}` pair (D3 applies inside restore
too — a restore can be clamped like any other write).

applied.description: What was written and what stuck.

oneOf.description: Already holding the recorded value; nothing was written.

The automation that owned this control when the snapshot was taken owns it again,
so its value is that automation's to choose — exactly as it was.

**A success**, and the distinction is not pedantry. Restoring an automation control
to "on" re-engages the manual control it governs, so on any device whose INACTIVE
flag follows the automation's value this is the *ordinary* outcome for every
guarded write's restore. Measured on the seed hardware the day
`controls --discover-pairs` first ran: the probe put the camera back perfectly and
then reported two controls it "could not put back", because the vocabulary had no
way to say "its owner is back". See note N9.

automation.description: The automation control that holds it, when the pair set names one.

oneOf.description: Could not be put back, and why.

outcomes.description: One entry per snapshotted control, in the order they were attempted.

Sample.description: One sample: a value, what the device actually took, the photo, and the scores.

applied.description:
The value the device actually holds — D3 applies inside sweeps too [PF:6], and a
sample labeled with a value the camera never held would poison every comparison
built on it.

photo.description:
The photo, as a path relative to the session directory — so a session directory
relocates as a unit.

requested.description: The value the sweep asked for.

oneOf.description: A built-in metric ranked the samples.
An agent reviewed the sample photos and picked one.
A human did.

criteria.description:
Ordered criteria for judging a sample. Recorded because the *selector* needs
them, whether that selector is a human, an agent, or a metric.

fingerprint.description: Which camera this was recorded against.

goal.description: What the session is trying to achieve, in the operator's words.

id.description: The session's identity — a UUIDv7, so directory listings sort chronologically.

notes.description:
Free-text notes. v1 does not pretend to model that focus and exposure interact;
it lets the operator write it down.

pre_snapshot.description:
The control state as found, persisted **before** the first write so a crashed
sweep is recoverable (design §6, gate G3).

queue.description:
The control queue, in the order the operator wants them calibrated. Reorderable
between sweeps.

schema_version.description:
The document version. Present from day one; a foreign version is a typed refusal
(design D9), never a best-effort parse.

task.description: The task, as the operator described it.

task_slug.description: The task through the slug transform — the directory name.

tool_version.description: The tool version that wrote it.

SettlePolicy.description:
A settle policy: the spec plus the deadline that bounds it.

Both forms are bounded, because "skip 10 frames" on a camera delivering none is a
hang, and a hang is the failure mode E3 warns about wearing a disguise.

deadline_ms.description: How long the whole settle may take.

SettleSpec.description: How long to wait for the sensor to settle before taking a photo [PF:11].

oneOf.description: Discard this many frames first.
Keep discarding frames for this long.

Sink.description:
Where binary results go (design D10).

Two variants, because a daemon and an in-process CLI need different answers and
pretending otherwise is how `-o out.jpg` ends up meaning the server's cwd. Clients
resolve relative paths against their own cwd *before* sending.

oneOf.description: Send the bytes back in the response.
Write them to an absolute path on whichever host runs the engine.

Snapshot.description: Every writable control's value at one instant.

camera.description:
Which camera it came from — restoring a snapshot onto a different camera is a
[`crate::Error::FingerprintMismatch`], not a surprise.

id.description:
Its kernel id, so restore does not depend on the slug transform being stable
across versions.

role.description:
Its role in restore ordering, decided from the pairing set when the snapshot was
taken.

was_inactive.description:
Whether the device reported it INACTIVE at snapshot time [PF:3] — such a control
is restored on the second pass.

was_volatile.description:
Whether the device reported it VOLATILE. A volatile value cannot be meaningfully
restored, and restore says so rather than pretending it did.

StreamRequest.description:
What a caller wants from a stream. Every field is optional: "just give me something"
is a legitimate request, and the answer is always reported back.

SweepSpec.description: How to derive the values a sweep visits.

oneOf.description: Every step from min to max. Capped by [`limits::MAX_SWEEP_SAMPLES`].
Every `step`-th value, aligned to the control's own step.

Logarithmically spaced, for controls like exposure time whose useful range
spans orders of magnitude.
Exactly these values.

Transform.description:
An orientation transform (the skill's flip and rotate).

On the verbatim-JPEG sink these become an EXIF Orientation tag — zero re-encode,
byte fidelity preserved (E6). On PNG and re-encode sinks they are applied to
pixels.

The serde spelling and [`Transform::as_str`] are the same strings on purpose: a
`--transform` argument and a `"transform"` field in a JSON document must name the
same thing the same way, and the CLI reaches this vocabulary rather than deriving
a second one of its own.

oneOf.description: Leave the image as the camera framed it.
Mirror horizontally.
Mirror vertically.
Rotate a quarter turn clockwise.
Rotate a half turn.
Rotate a quarter turn counter-clockwise.

TransformApplication.description:
Where a requested orientation ended up.

"The photo is rotated" and "the photo says it is rotated" are different facts, and a
viewer that ignores EXIF distinguishes them — so the answer records which happened
rather than leaving the caller to infer it from the sink.

oneOf.description: Nothing was asked for.
The pixels were rotated or mirrored before encoding.

The pixels were left alone and the orientation rides in EXIF, so the bitstream
stays verbatim (E6).

UnrestorableReason.description: Why one control could not be put back.

oneOf.description:
The control has been taken over by automation that did **not** hold it when the
snapshot was taken.

A real change we could not undo, and distinct from
[`RestoreOutcome::OwnedByAutomation`], which is the same *flag* meaning the
opposite thing: there, the owner is the one that was there before.

automation.description: The automation partner, when one is known.

oneOf.description: The control reports VOLATILE: its value is the device's to choose.
The control has gone read-only, or vanished, since the snapshot.
The write failed. The error rides along so the caller can act on it.

Unverifiable.description:
Why a write could not be read back.

Both members are read off the descriptor the device supplied, so neither is a
guess about the device's intentions.

oneOf.description:
The control's type has no value: `V4L2_CTRL_TYPE_BUTTON` is a trigger, and
writing it *is* the effect.

The device flags the control `WRITE_ONLY`, which is the device saying that
reading it would not mean anything.

The write was accepted and the read-back that should have followed it was
refused by the device.

Distinct from the two above because it is not a property of the descriptor:
nothing said this control was unreadable, and then it was. Several drivers
answer `EINVAL` to `G_EXT_CTRLS` for controls they happily enumerate, so this
is a real outcome rather than a defensive branch — and it is the one case
where a caller might sensibly re-read later.

WriteReport.description:
What `set` answers (design D3/E4).

A list rather than a single [`Applied`], because a guarded write is more than one
write: switching an automation partner off is a change to the camera the caller is
entitled to see, and hiding it would make `--guarded` a verb whose side effects are
undocumented at the moment they happen.

disabled_automation.description:
The automation controls that were switched off to make the rest stick.

Derived from the plan rather than from the writes, so it stays a statement about
intent: a caller restoring the camera afterwards needs the list even when one of
the switch-offs was itself adjusted.

writes.description:
Every write the plan made, in the order it made them — the automation switch-offs
included, each with its own `{requested, applied}` pair.

WriteWarning.description:
A warning that rides a successful write.

Not an error: the driver accepted the write and reported success. But the caller
asked for one thing and got another, and D13 keeps warnings out of the error registry
precisely so a warning is never mistaken for a failure.

oneOf.description: The driver clamped the value into range and said "success" [PF:6].

range.description: The range it was clamped into, as declared at write time.

oneOf.description: The driver aligned the value to the control's step.

step.description: The step it was aligned to.

oneOf.description:
The value came back different for a reason we cannot attribute. Still reported:
an unexplained difference is the most interesting kind.

The write was accepted and there was nothing to read back, so
[`Applied::applied`] is what was *asked for* rather than what was observed.

D3 says every write reads back. Some controls cannot: a `BUTTON` is a trigger with
no value, and a `WRITE_ONLY` control's value is the device's to keep. Returning
`{requested, applied}` with the two equal and no warning would make those writes
indistinguishable from verified ones, which is the collapse E4 exists to prevent —
so the gap is carried as data instead.
